text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended higher on talk of Russian buying. Further details were not immediately available. August closed 60 cents higher at $319.00 per tonne, while October added 40 cents to close at $308.60 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended a quiet session higher with front month July adding 7 points to close at 11.05 cents/lb, while October added 5 points to close at 10.84 cents/lb. Traders said memorial day and a dearth of fundamental news will keep players sidelined for this week. FUNDAMENTALS

TAIWAN - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 31,503 tonnes, raw value, compared to negligible amounts in February 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996/97 (November/February) up to 31,550 tonnes compared to 10 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 124,079 tonnes against 125,386 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of origin in November/February 1996/97 was Australia with 31,500 tonnes raws against nil.

Sugar exports in November/February 1996/97 reached 18,934 tonnes compared to negligible amounts in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 25,562 tonnes against 14,782 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in November/February 1996/97 was the USA with 18,862 tonnes raws against nil.

SWITZERLAND - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 8,403 tonnes, raw value, down from 13,965 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 59,534 tonnes against 78,682 tonnes in the first half of 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 169,593 tonnes against 155,620 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/March 1996/97 were Germany with 41,250 tonnes whites against 49,211 tonnes and France with 11,115 tonnes compared to 20,861 tonnes.

GERMANY - Sugar imports in January 1997 amounted to 8,137 tonnes, raw value, down from 17,685 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) up to 78,182 tonnes, slightly up on the 71,909 tonnes imported in the like period a year ago. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 206,911 tonnes against 225,848 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were France with 54,130 tonnes whites against 52,830 tonnes and the Netherlands with 7,482 tonnes, up from 5,667 tonnes.

Sugar exports in January 1997 amounted to 127,295 tonnes compared to 99,839 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/January 1996/97 up to 664,006 tonnes compared to 652,450 tonnes in October/January 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 1.316 million tonnes compared to 1.452 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Belgium-Luxembourg with 92,692 tonnes whites against 70,434 tonnes, Italy with 96,832 tonnes, up from 27,814 tonnes, the United Arab Emirates with 84,859 tonnes, down from 121,865 tonnes and Switzerland with 33,494 tonnes against 43,546 tonnes.

EUROPE - Western Europe's sugar beet areas remained in a rainy pattern during the week ended May 20 which favoured beet development. Vegetative development will continue to progress favorably. Eastern Europe has been turning steadily drier at the same time. Moisture supplies are becoming short in some of the southern areas of this region and with a potential for more dry weather the crop could start to suffer stress. The region will have to see rains increase by the beginning of June to avoid losses of yield potential.

Dryness in the beet growing areas in the former Soviet Union in May has aided planting activity and helped get the crop off to a favourable start. However, soil moisture supplies are quickly declining and rains are needed.

CUBA - Unidentified Cuban sources said that 1996/97 production would be no more than 4.2 million tonnes, tel quel, down from 4.45 million tonnes produced the previous year. This is likely to support prices, although it was known for quite some time that this year's crop is in difficulties.
